look_here_first: Start with the compound leaf: many narrow lance-shaped leaflets sit along a conspicuously winged rachis. Then confirm the deciduous, clonal shrub/small-tree habit and vivid red fall color.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: many narrow lanceolate leaflets on an odd-pinnate leaf

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: rachis conspicuously winged between leaflet pairs

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: deciduous clonal shrub or small tree with vivid red/orange fall foliage

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: dense terminal panicles produce dark-red hairy flattened drupes

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Deciduous, thicket-forming shrub or small tree.

key_traits.label: Leaf morphology
key_traits.text: Usually about 13–21 narrow lanceolate leaflets; upper surface darker/glossier, lower surface paler to hairy.

key_traits.label: Rachis
key_traits.text: Strongly winged between leaflet pairs — one of the fastest field characters.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Dark-red hairy flattened drupes in dense pyramidal clusters.

key_traits.label: Joey field observation
key_traits.text: Joey Santore video frame labeled Rhus lanceolata shows the compound-leaved small-tree habit; current project taxonomy reconciles that source name to Rhus copallinum var. lanceolata.
